slides.0.title: Key White Grape Varieties
slides.0.subtitle: Assyrtiko and the native whites
slides.1.title: White wine leads in Greece
slides.1.highlights.0.title: About 70% of output is white
slides.1.highlights.0.content: High acidity and ample sun give white wines a vivid style
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Grapes in this lesson
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Assyrtiko, Moschofilero, Malagousia, Roditis, Savatiano, Athiri, Aidani, Robola, Vidiano
slides.1.content: Method: for each grape, remember region + aroma + acidity/structure.
slides.2.title: Assyrtiko: the flagship white
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Home: Santorini
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Most characteristic on volcanic soil; now planted across the Aegean and mainland Greece
slides.2.highlights.1.title: High acid, mineral
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Keeps high acidity even at full ripeness; on nutrient-poor Santorini soils pH can be very low
slides.2.highlights.2.title: A stylistic spectrum
slides.2.highlights.2.content: From fresh steel-fermented to oaked and lees-aged, up to sweet Vinsanto
slides.2.content: PDO Santorini permits blends of Assyrtiko with Athiri and Aidani, with Assyrtiko dominant.
slides.3.title: Aromatic white varieties
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Moschofilero
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Pink-skinned, made as white; Mantinia plateau; intense floral aromas, pale lemon-pink, vibrant acidity
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Malagousia
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Peach, lemon zest and floral notes; nearly lost, rediscovered around Epanomi, first varietal bottling in 1986
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Vidiano
slides.3.highlights.2.content: A Cretan grape; peach, apricot, melon, honey and herbs; acidity holds even at higher alcohol
slides.3.content: In Diploma blind tasting Moschofilero and Malagousia are told apart as aromatic whites: Moschofilero leans rose and high acid, Malagousia peach and citrus zest.
slides.4.title: Widely planted and traditional grapes
slides.4.highlights.0.title: Savatiano
slides.4.highlights.0.content: The workhorse of Central Greece and Attica, traditionally used for Retsina
slides.4.highlights.1.title: Roditis
slides.4.highlights.1.content: Pink-skinned and widely planted (e.g. in the Peloponnese); a fresh style
slides.4.highlights.2.title: Athiri and Aidani
slides.4.highlights.2.content: Traditional Aegean island grapes, often blended with Assyrtiko
slides.4.highlights.3.title: Robola
slides.4.content: Each of these four is tied to a terroir tag: Attica/Retsina, the Peloponnese, the Aegean islands, Cephalonia.
slides.5.componentProps.slide.title: 🧠 Knowledge Check
Which white, known for high acidity and minerality, comes from Santorini?
Assyrtiko is Greece's most internationally recognised white grape.
Which pink-skinned grape made as white grows on the Mantinia plateau?
Moschofilero is known for rose-like floral aroma and vibrant acidity.
Which grape is traditionally used for Retsina?
Savatiano is widely planted in Attica and Central Greece and is the traditional base for Retsina.
